medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Office of Student Affairs provides comprehensive support services for medical students at HWCOM. Academic Counseling and Enrichment Services (ACES) supports students through personalized learning strategies and peer-assisted instruction. The office includes two Medical Education Learning Specialists, known as Academic Enrichment Counselors (AECs), and the Supplemental Peer Instruction (SPI) program. Students can meet one-on-one with an AEC for individualized academic support. The SPI program offers peer tutoring to strengthen understanding of course material. AECs and SPIs also lead workshops and group sessions on time management, adapting to the medical curriculum, and board exam preparation.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may request a voluntary leave of absence (LOA) for academic, financial, medical, or personal reasons. If a student wishes to pursue a voluntary LOA, he or she should consult with the Associate Dean for Student Affairs and/or the HWCOM Registrar to review the process. The maximum amount of time granted for leaves of absence is 12 months. The Executive Associate Dean for Student Affairs (or designee) and the Executive Associate Dean for Academic Affairs (or designee) are responsible for granting or denying requests.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Panther Learning Communities (PLCs) enhance the medical school experience by maximizing learning through co-curricular activities. There are four PLCs, each comprised of medical students from all classes. The PLCs sponsor three signature programs: MedLEAD, Culinary Medicine Program and Community Service Learning in collaboration with NeighborhoodHELP. HWCOM sponsors the Medical Student Council (MSC), which funds specialty focused programming and serves as the voice of the student body. Students have the opportunity to join national organizations and specialty interest groups. HWCOM has chapters of Alpha Omega Alpha Honor Medical Society and the Gold Humanism Honor Society. In addition, HWCOM has a Phi Delta Epsilon International Medical Fraternity and Rotaract Chapter; both which focus to create physicians of integrity through fellowship in service, leadership, and professional mentoring.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Located in Miami, a major international and cultural center, FIU is a vibrant, student-centered public research university that is worlds ahead in its commitment to learning, research, entrepreneurship, innovation, and creativity. The 344-acre Modesto A. Maidique Campus, where Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine is housed, is only minutes from Miami International Airport, the Port of Miami, cultural centers, outdoor recreation, sporting events, schools, shopping, and beautiful beaches. Clinical experiences occur in public and private health care facilities throughout South Florida.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Most medical students choose to live near the Modesto A. Maidique Campus where Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine is housed, while others live in surrounding areas throughout Miami such as Doral, Kendall, Brickell, South Miami, Coconut Grove, and Coral Gables. For more information about off-campus residential options, applicants and students can visit classifieds.fiu.edu.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: FIU Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine supports LGBTQIA+ students through student-led and institutional initiatives. Medical Students for Gender and Sexuality Advancement (Med GSA) promote awareness of gender- and sexuality-related health issues, builds peer support, and strengthens competency in inclusive patient care. The Office of Student Affairs offers confidential counseling and well-being services tailored to medical students, including support related to identity, stress, and professional growth. The college maintains a respectful learning environment through non-discrimination policies protecting students based on gender identity and sexual orientation, with clear reporting and support pathways. In addition, the FIU Pride Center and university resources provide campus programming, education, and community engagement that foster inclusion and connection.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The FIU Disability Resource Center (DRC) is responsible for assisting students with obtaining appropriate and reasonable academic accommodations based on a documented disability. It is the responsibility of the student who needs accommodations to register with the FIU DRC to receive accommodations. Any student who fails to complete the registration process with DRC will not receive accommodations to meet HWCOM professional and technical standards. Students are accountable for their performance, with or without accommodations. All technical and academic standards need to be met with or without reasonable accommodations. The Assistant Dean for Student Success and Wellbeing within the Office of Student Affairs is a point of contact for students should they have any questions regarding accommodations or accessing DRC.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The Office of Student Affairs provides robust student support services for the medical students at HWCOM. The Academic Counseling and Enrichment Services (ACES) is designed to support medical students in their academic journey through personalized learning strategies and peer-assisted instruction. The office comprises two Medical Education Learning Specialists, known as Academic Enrichment Counselors (AECs), along with the Supplemental Peer Instruction (SPI) program. Students who are struggling academically or seeking to enhance their learning strategies can meet one-on-one with an AEC to develop personalized approaches for success. Additionally, the SPI program offers one-on-one peer tutoring, providing students with opportunities to collaborate with a tutor, whether they need extra support or simply want to refine their understanding of course material. Beyond individual services, the AECs and SPIs team provide workshops, presentations, and group sessions on key topics, including time management, adjusting to medical school curriculum, and how to prepare for board exams. The Student Wellbeing and Mental Health Services (SWMHS) Office is dedicated to promoting the wellbeing and mental health of our medical students. The office is staffed by a full-time licensed clinical psychologist and a full-time licensed therapist, both of whom operate independently of student academics, ensuring that they have no role in assessment or grading. Services include individual psychotherapy, couples therapy, psychoeducational assessments, and holistic wellness interventions such as aromatherapy, and mind-body practices. Beyond individual services, the SWMHS team provides wellbeing programing through workshops, sessions, and presentations throughout students' medical training on key topics, including adjusting to medical school, managing burnout, self-care, and resilience-building.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The HWCOM family values educational excellence, innovation, inclusion, integrity, and service. Each of us is responsible for upholding these high ideals. We do so by fostering a culture of respect between teachers, learners, and staff. Further, we carry these ideals out into the community, working with our partners to make a positive impact on the world around us.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Clinical and other learning experiences occur at various locations across South Florida.  Public transportation is not readily available to all sites.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: All medical students are expected to convey a professional demeanor, not only in their behavior but also in their dress and appearance.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Academic success support services are robust and include academic advising, personal counseling, learning specialist services, peer tutoring, recording of formal instruction, and skills training.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Clinical experiences begin within the first three months of study.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Instruction styles include lecture, laboratory, simulation, flipped classroom, case- and problem-based group discussions, team-based learning sessions, clinical experiences, and independent study.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations take place in numerous health care systems throughout South Florida, including both public and private hospitals and outpatient sites.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: A guided background preparation is offered, but not required.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Rank is used to identify students eligible for AOA, but is not reported on the transcript or in the MSPE.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is required for activities requiring student participation, for example case discussions and team-based learning sessions. Attendance is not required for lecture-only, recorded sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The course of study leading to the MD degree is based on development of the medical knowledge, skills, values, and behaviors required for the practice of medicine. The educational program is broad and general, preparing students for postgraduate study in their chosen field of medical specialization, licensure, and medical practice. Course work is multidisciplinary. Clinical experiences in primary care begins during the first academic year. The curriculum includes formal study in the development of professional attributes and knowledge of health care systems, policy, law, medical ethics, and advancement of medical knowledge and practice through research and scholarship. Students are engaged with households and communities in a longitudinal service-learning program in collaboration with FIU students from other health professions. The program concludes with a capstone of intense preparation for entry into residency.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The HWCOM curriculum reflects a broad approach to training in patient care and a commitment to improving health in the community. The college’s longitudinal curriculum in community medicine, NeighborhoodHELP, provides opportunities for engagement among medical students, families, and communities. Students work with families and communities over the full course of the MD program. The goals of the program are to improve the health of families and communities while developing the students’ skills and knowledge. These hands-on experiences greatly enhance students’ ability to care for all populations of patients by broadening student understanding of the factors that affect personal and community health.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Fostering research to discover and advance medically relevant knowledge is integral to the mission of HWCOM. Numerous research opportunities are available for medical students both as curricular and non-curricular research projects.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: The program spans sequential periods of study of unequal length and includes 5 integrated strands  (Human Biology and Disease, Clinical Medicine, Professional Behavior, Medicine & Society, & Research)
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Community service is a requirement incorporated into the formal curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Study in medical research and scholarship is a required part of the curriculum and is facilitated through the longitudinal Research Scholarship Course.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: HWCOM has primary clinical affiliation agreements with Baptist Hospital South Florida and Nicklaus Children’s Hospital and partners with numerous other clinical affiliates.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Courses are graded pass/fail. Core clinical clerkships are graded honors/pass/fail. Fourth year courses and clerkships are graded pass/fail. Honors may be achieved in each of the five strands.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine (HWCOM) at FIU is a community-based, twenty-first-century medical school located in Miami, Florida, with an innovative medical education curriculum. The 4-year course of study leading to the Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree allows students to gain the competencies expected of all physicians along with an emphasis on social accountability. The program is designed to maximize exposure and training in all areas of medical education and prepares students for postgraduate study in any specialty, for licensure, and for future medical practice. Students receive hands-on experience observing and caring for families in the community who have little or no access to medical care. The medical training students receive occurs at a variety of public and private inpatient and outpatient clinical settings, emphasizing the importance of the doctor-patient relationship in diverse patient populations.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine develops highly qualified, community-engaged, socially accountable health care professionals and serves our region, our nation and the greater world through transformative translational research, medical education and clinical programs that drive forward innovations in health care.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
The 7-year (3+4) BS/M.D. program is designed for outstanding high school students interested in attending medical school at Florida International University.

The program is a collaboration between the College of Arts, Sciences & Education, Honors College and Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine that allows exceptional students to earn both a Bachelor of Science in Biological Sciences and Doctor of Medicine in seven years, a shorter amount of time than typically required for both degrees.

Students displaying a strong academic background, demonstrated leadership, community service and health care experiences will have the potential for guaranteed admission to the College of Medicine starting in their fourth year of the program, provided they meet all requirements.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: HWCOM requires level I and level II criminal background checks.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Letters of recommendation from friends or relatives are not considered. In all cases, letters should be recent and from individuals who can assess an applicant’s personal qualities. Letters must be written on official letterhead stationary and signed.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: HWCOM requires a minimum of three letters of recommendation, two from science faculty (biology, chemistry, physics, and math) and one from any other faculty member who has taught the applicant. In addition to the required letters, applicants can submit up to three supplemental letters from physicians, researchers, mentors, and employers who know the applicant well.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: All interviews for the 2026-2027 cycle will be conducted virtually. For more information on the virtual interview process please visit: https://medicine.fiu.edu/academics/doctor-of-medicine/admissions/application-process-a-z/index.html
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: HWCOM uses the semi-blind interview format, in which the interviewer has access to selected information from the application. Each applicant has two separate one-on-one interviews. All interviews conducted on Zoom virtually.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo:
All AMCAS verified applicants. 
There is no screening.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Students seeking Early Decision admission must apply only to HWCOM on AMCAS by the deadline. Candidates must meet the following minimum academic criteria: Overall GPA 3.70, BCPM 3.50, MCAT 510.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: HWCOM is committed to the education of students from Florida. Applicants will not, however, be limited to candidates from Florida. Only U.S. Citizens and U.S. Permanent Residents will be considered.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Residency reclassification for tuition purposes is governed by Section 1009.21 of the Florida Statues. Policies regarding reclassification are listed in the HWCOM Medical Student Handbook.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Each Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine (HWCOM) applicant must:
1. Be a citizen or permanent resident of the United States
2. Have a bachelor's degree at the time of matriculation
3. Have completed the required prerequisite courses at the time of matriculation
4. Have taken the Medical College Admission Test (MCAT)
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: There is no minimum undergraduate GPA for consideration.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: There is no minimum number of credit hours to be eligible for consideration.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Lower division pre-requisite courses can be taken at community colleges. However, additional upper level science courses are encouraged in preparation for the MCAT and success in medical school.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
We accept updates pertaining to new experiences and/or activities you have participated in since application submission. Please note that we do not accept and/or consider updates pertaining to grades that were not verified by AMCAS.

If you wish to submit an application update regarding your new experiences and/or activities, please log into your Application Portal ( https://admissions.medicine.fiu.edu ) with your AMCAS ID number and password and visit the "Documents" tab to upload an update directly to your application.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Students must be able to complete all requirements for the M.D. degree. In addition to strong academic performance and personal qualities, students are expected to have the knowledge and skills to perform effectively in diverse clinical settings & provide comprehensive patient care as outlined in the curriculum. Candidates for the M.D. degree must be able to fully and promptly perform essential functions in each of the six categories outlined in the Technical Standards, with or without reasonable accommodations. These abilities must be demonstrated independently—without relying on technology or intermediaries that compromise direct observation, judgment, or decision-making. The use of a trained intermediary is generally not permitted in clinical settings. Students with disabilities who may need reasonable accommodations to meet these standards are encouraged to request them in accordance with FIU Medicine and university policies.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The HWCOM Office of Financial Assistance provides support to students in achieving their educational aspirations while successfully managing their finances and is committed to providing students with the best possible financial resources, counseling, and customer service throughout their medical education. The Office of Financial Assistance provides counseling to prospective and current students from preadmission to graduation. They maintain an open door policy and meet with students who want more information about financial aid, personal budgeting, debt management, or other financial issues. Several financial aid and scholarship options are available to medical students, such as the HWCOM Graduate Need Grant, institutional and private scholarships, and federal and private student loans. HWCOM students can begin the financial aid application process by completing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at www.fafsa.gov. The FIU school code for financial aid is 009635.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: FIU HWCOM tuition and fees are established by the Florida State Legislature, Florida Board of Governors, and the FIU Board of Trustees. In accordance with FIU policy, the university will refund tuition and fees for Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine students as follows: 100 percent of tuition and fees will be refunded if the student officially withdraws or is dismissed from HWCOM in writing before the last day of Orientation; 50 percent of the tuition will be refunded if the student officially withdraws or is dismissed from HWCOM in writing before the end of the fourth week of classes per term; 25 percent of the tuition will be refunded if the student officially withdraws or is dismissed from HWCOM in writing before the end of the sixth week of classes per term.

medSchoolPrograms.info: Students in period three of medical study may apply to the MBA, MPH or Master of Science in Health Informatics and Analytics (MSHIA) programs. Combined degree students complete the first 3 years of coursework in the MD degree program. At the beginning of the 4th period of study, students admitted to another degree pause their medical studies and begin classes in the MBA, MPH or MSHIA program. Classes in the MBA program are taken during fall and spring semesters of the medical student’s fourth year of study (33 credit hours) as well as the summer for the MPH and MSHIA programs (36 and 27 credits respectively). Nine credits taken through HWCOM are applied toward the 42 credits required for the MBA degree, toward the 45 credits for the MPH and 10 credits toward the 37 credit MSHIA program. At the beginning of the 5th year, students resume study as part of the MD degree program and those who successfully complete all requirements graduate with a combined degree at the end of the 5 years.

medSchoolPrograms.name: Combined Doctor of Medicine and Master of Science in Health Informatics and Analysis (MD/MSHIA)
medSchoolPrograms.programLength: At the beginning of their fourth period of medical study, students admitted to the combined program pause their medical studies and begin classes as part of the MSHIA program. They take MSHIA classes during their fourth year's fall, spring, and early summer semesters to complete the 27 hours of MSHIA coursework. Additionally, ten credits taken at the Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine are applied toward the 37 credits required for the MSHIA degree.
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: FIU students may apply to the combined MD/MSHIA program in their third period of medical study. However, please note that each college independently reviews and admits applicants to their programs. And only students admitted to both programs can enroll in classes in the combined program.

medSchoolPrograms.name: FIU Stempel College of Public Health and Social Work
medSchoolPrograms.programLength: 3 Semesters; The program begins in August and ends in June.
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: Students apply in the Fall or Early Spring semester of their third year in medical school, must be in good academic standing, and must receive approval from the Medical Student Evaluation and Promotion Committee, the HWCOM Office of Student Affairs, and the HWCOM Office Medical Education.

medSchoolPrograms.info: Doctors of Tomorrow (DOT) Program is an intensive 6-day residential premedical program for highly motivated college students who are Florida Residents. The DOT Program includes activities that span the following areas: academic enrichment, learning skills development, communication skills, counseling, career development and character building and enrichment activities. The focus is on helping participants to develop the knowledge, skills, experiences, and attributes to be a competitive medical school applicant. For more information, please visit https://medicine.fiu.edu/academics/degrees-and-programs/doctor-of-medicine/pre-med-programs/doctors-of-tomorrow/index.html

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The Admissions Committee votes to accept, not accept, or place an applicant on the Wait List. Applicants are offered a seat on a rolling basis. The Wait List remains active until Orientation.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Prerequisite courses must be completed in the United States or Canada. Substitutions for required courses will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Prerequisite courses do not expire although the Admissions Committee would prefer to see recent upper division coursework if prerequisite courses were completed years ago.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Admissions Committee uses the American Medical College Application Service, the HWCOM secondary application, letters of recommendation, and interview feedback to select applicants who have demonstrated well-rounded, rigorous academic preparation; character and maturity; and who best suit the HWCOM mission. Applicants must demonstrate a strong interest in medicine and must have a record of personal experiences suggesting medical care exposure, research, altruism, integrity, community service, and leadership, with the ability and desire to pursue lifelong learning. Most important are the personal attributes necessary to be a competent, compassionate physician. Presently, only U.S. Citizens and U.S. Permanent Residents are considered.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Exposure to clinical medicine, such as physician shadowing and hands-on patient care activities is highly encouraged.
